clue.text: Drinking quickly, setter unsteady somewhere in London

parts.note: to down a drink is to swallow it in one go

indicators.note: something unsteady wobbles out of position, so these letters do not stay in their printed order

parts.note: the letters of the word as printed, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter, knocking back drinks too fast, is wobbling about somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinking quickly' gives DOWNING, then SETTER is rearranged into STREET. Downing Street is where the British Prime Minister lives, at Number 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing Street is a famous road in Westminster, so it is one particular location within the British capital.

clue.text: Last longer than most of your stat might suggest?

indicators.note: taking most but not all of a word means its final letter is dropped
the letters only hint at the result, which must be found by rearranging them freely

parts.note: the word with its last letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's statistics claim they will endure longer than they actually will.
explanation.walkthrough: YOU plus STAT, seven letters, rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to remain somewhere beyond a set time or beyond another person, so it means outlasting.

clue.text: Hitman in Japan's hidden?

indicators.note: the word says outright that something is concealed inside the letters of the clue

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and into the third

explanation.surface: A question about whether a contract killer is lying low in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'hitmaN IN JApan'; the question mark nods to the definition being a loose one, and to the ninja itself being a hidden figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a covert Japanese agent hired for espionage and assassination, so loosely a paid killer.

clue.text: 'Hulk' not half succeeds on getting reboot: chance'd be a fine thing

indicators.note: keeping only half a word means the back four of its eight letters are thrown away
a reboot of a film franchise remakes the material in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
no and not both express negation
the first half of the word

explanation.surface: A remake of the Hulk film is only half successful: the hoped-for reboot is wishful thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: HULK, NO and SUCC are pooled and rearranged; 'on getting' simply links that wordplay to the phrase meaning wishful thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are rueful idioms said when something wished for is unlikely ever to happen.

clue.text: One mason's silent, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letters of each word are used

parts.note: the two central letters of the six
the two central letters of the six

explanation.surface: A Freemason keeps quiet, as is basically required of him.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Masonic secrecy, but 'essentially' just asks for the core of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or only, the one and no other, as in 'the sole survivor'.

clue.text: Light vehicle strains to turn left

parts.note: a rick is a sprain or wrench of a joint
haw is the command to a horse or ox to turn left

explanation.surface: A small car labours as it steers to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strains' looks like a verb about the vehicle's effort, but it is a noun meaning sprains. Haw is an old ploughman's call telling the animal to go left.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a small two-wheeled passenger cart, pulled or pedalled, so a lightweight conveyance.

clue.text: With times moving on, that may be seen to become timeless

parts.words: With times moving on, that may be seen to become
parts.note: surface reading: something that survives as the years pass
setter's reading: what endures without end is beyond time altogether

explanation.surface: As the years roll by, some things come to be regarded as classics.
explanation.walkthrough: A thing that keeps lasting while the ages pass earns the label of something without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe what exists without beginning or end, unaffected by the passing of ages.

clue.text: Freaks of nature: mongrels ain't regularly included

indicators.note: to be included is to be taken inside something else

parts.note: mutts are dogs of mixed breed

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept, skipping the rest

parts.note: first and third letters

explanation.surface: A rant that oddballs of the natural world do not count crossbred dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ain't is skipped when taking alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutant is an organism changed by genetic mutation, an aberration from its species' normal form.

clue.text: Groom with 'Mad Men' stylings, like a fancy hanky?

indicators.note: styling something is restyling it, giving its material a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bridegroom dressed in the sharp 1960s fashion of the TV series Mad Men, complete with a dandyish pocket square.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a smart handkerchief is often stitched with initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A monogrammed item is embroidered with the owner's initials, typical of a smart pocket handkerchief.

clue.text: A bit of ghastly cheese and fruit

indicators.note: a bit is a portion, so only part of the following letters is taken

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into most of the second

explanation.surface: A cheeseboard with a nasty piece of cheese next to some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of ghastly cheese' reads like a portion of food, but it marks the letters ghastLY CHEESe.
explanation.definitionFit: Lychees are small sweet Asian fruits with a rough red shell and white flesh.

clue.text: Pop quintet is short, stunted family group

indicators.note: a stunted plant never reaches full growth, so the word is denied its final letter

parts.note: Steps were a five-piece British pop group of the late 1990s
taken as written
terse means brief or curt

explanation.surface: A comment that a five-piece band is brief and stunted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like the cutting signal, but it is the synonym TERSE; 'stunted' does the cutting. Steps were a British pop band of five singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepsisters are daughters of a step-parent, so a set of them is a group of relations by marriage.

clue.text: Greek character to provide roof for bird

parts.note: nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
to thatch is to cover a roof with straw or reeds

explanation.surface: A Greek person sets out to build a shelter for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small songbird that climbs tree trunks headfirst and wedges nuts into bark.

clue.text: Perhaps hearing report of euro's make-up

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the answer is how the words are spoken

parts.note: a euro is made up of one hundred cents

explanation.surface: Perhaps a hearing considers an account of how the euro was formed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a tribunal, but it is an example of one of the five faculties, as 'perhaps' warns.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing is one of the five senses, with sight, touch, taste and smell, so it is an example.

clue.text: Fertiliser reserves upset man's invested in somewhere in Cuba

indicators.note: money invested in a business goes into it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: guano is seabird or bat droppings used as manure
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, which in a down clue turns the letters upside down

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Stocks of manure are disturbed when a man puts money into a Cuban location.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of man's stands for 'is', linking the pieces to the container signal. TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Guantanamo Bay is on the south-eastern coast of Cuba, home to a US naval base.

clue.text: Painter (grand), returned a casual greeting

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a plus yo, an informal hello

explanation.surface: A great painter answers someone's offhand hello.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'grand' look like praise of the artist, but it gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was a Spanish artist of the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

clue.text: Novel about brash strongman

parts.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
loud and brash both mean showy or overbearing
Atlas was the Titan who held up the sky

explanation.surface: A story about an overbearing muscleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the link between book and subject, but it is the abbreviation for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud Atlas is a 2004 book by David Mitchell, later filmed, so it is a piece of fiction.

clue.text: Timidity caught by ancient poetry

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
old and ancient both mean of great age
feet are the metrical units that make up lines of verse

explanation.surface: Shyness is captured in old verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught by' reads as captured within, but it is a single letter placed first. C for caught comes from cricket scoring, a bat-and-ball game popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting cold feet is an idiom for losing nerve, so the phrase names a loss of courage.

clue.text: Household devices prepared cold salmon

indicators.note: food that is prepared is cut up and rearranged before serving

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitchen gadgets have made a chilled fish dish ready.
explanation.walkthrough: All mod cons, short for all modern conveniences, is a British estate agents' phrase for appliances such as washing machines and central heating.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers the modern conveniences of a home, such as appliances and heating, so household equipment.

clue.text: Everyman, blood pressure rising in the French lake with Frenchman wanting protection from elements

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: la is French for the, in the feminine
L is the map abbreviation for lake
M is short for monsieur
the setter refers to himself, so I

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards, so the order flips

parts.note: the standard medical abbreviation

explanation.surface: The setter's blood pressure climbs at a French lake with a Frenchman, wanting shelter from the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns only the blood pressure abbreviation, and the setter's own pronoun sits ahead of it inside the French article. Monsieur, French for Mr, shortens to M.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip balm is a waxy salve that shields the lips from wind, cold and sun, the weather's elements.

clue.text: To be heard, provoke ravens' calls

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the answer only has to sound right

parts.note: to cause something is to provoke it

explanation.surface: Needling the birds so that they cry out.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is spelt as the bird noise but spoken like the verb meaning bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: A caw is the harsh cry of a crow, rook or raven, so plural cries of these birds.

clue.text: Adriatic land, Balkan? Assigned name: Illyria? Absolutely, at first!

definitions.text: Adriatic land, Balkan? Assigned name: Illyria? Absolutely, at first!

indicators.note: what comes at first is at the very start, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.words: Adriatic land, Balkan? Assigned name: Illyria? Absolutely
parts.note: the initials of the seven words

explanation.surface: A quiz exchange: is a Balkan country on the Adriatic once called Illyria? Yes, originally!
explanation.walkthrough: Every word before 'at first' contributes its first letter, and the whole clue also describes the country: Illyria was the ancient name for the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Albania is a Balkan state on the Adriatic coast whose territory roughly matches ancient Illyria.

clue.text: Light bike moved aimlessly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a low-powered motorised two-wheeler
second meaning: past tense of a verb for wandering about listlessly

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a bicycle wobbling about; the two halves are separate meanings, a noun and a past-tense verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a small motor scooter and, as a verb, means wandered about in a gloomy, listless way.

clue.text: I can be seen among bald men challenging part of bill

indicators.note: to be among others is to be surrounded by them
challenging things means upsetting their order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spotted in a group of hairless men, someone takes issue with part of a law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests legislation, but it is a bird's beak.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandible is either half of a bird's beak, upper or lower, so one section of it.

clue.text: Material extracted from ground, sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up makes it read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: ore extracted from the ground has been mined

explanation.surface: Stuff dug out of the earth is shipped upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' suggests raw ore, matching the mining picture, but it is cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy cotton twill fabric used for jeans, so a type of cloth.

clue.text: Listen to me: some apps stink

indicators.note: some means a part, so only a portion of the following letters is wanted

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone confides a grumble that certain phone apps are rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'Listen to me' a call for attention before a complaint; the letters sit in apPS STink.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is the hushed sound made to catch someone's attention discreetly, a whispered summons.

clue.text: What's seen in a chest, or somewhere below one?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the sliding boxes in a chest of furniture
second meaning: old-fashioned underpants, worn below a person's chest

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chest' is first a piece of furniture, then the body part: the second meaning is underwear worn lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the compartments of a chest of drawers and, dated, knickers or underpants.

clue.text: Shelters knight in an annexe with son

parts.note: an and a are the same article

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed within it

parts.note: a wing is an extension built onto a building
N is the chess notation for knight
the genealogical abbreviation

explanation.surface: A knight takes refuge in an outbuilding with his son.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation the knight is N, since K is already the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Awnings are canvas canopies stretched over windows or doors to keep off sun and rain, so covers.

clue.text: Mint tea I aim to turn into modern culinary proposition

indicators.note: turning something churns it over, so its letters change order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef plans to transform a herbal brew into a trendy new dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like part of the phrase 'aim to', but its letters belong to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant-based substitutes for meat are a recent food trend, so a fashionable offering on menus.
